title: Major obstetric haemorrhage
summary: Major antepartum, intrapartum, or postpartum haemorrhage with or without signs of shock.

mh-outcome.title: Major obstetric haemorrhage — emergency drill
actions: Call for help immediately — put out the major obstetric haemorrhage call per local protocol; call 999 if outside a hospital setting.
A–E assessment; high-flow oxygen; two large-bore IV cannulae; take bloods for FBC, coagulation, group & crossmatch, fibrinogen.
Start warmed IV crystalloid while awaiting blood products; activate massive transfusion protocol per local thresholds — VERIFY local trigger volumes.
For postpartum haemorrhage: rub up the fundus, empty the bladder (catheterise), and give uterotonics per local protocol/PGD — VERIFY drug, dose and sequence locally.
Identify and treat the cause using the 4 Ts: Tone (uterine atony), Trauma (genital tract), Tissue (retained placenta/products), Thrombin (coagulopathy).
For antepartum haemorrhage: do not perform digital vaginal examination until placenta praevia excluded; continuous fetal monitoring once available.
Keep a running total of estimated blood loss and call for senior obstetric/anaesthetic/haematology input early — do not wait for deterioration.
mh-outcome.phoneScript: If this is identified by phone (e.g. reported heavy bleeding at home): call 999 immediately, advise her to lie down with legs raised if able and not to drive, and stay on the line for further instructions.
documentationPrompts: Time bleeding identified/reported and time help called.
Interventions given (fluids, uterotonics, blood products) with times and doses.
Cause identified (4 Ts) and definitive management.
